newsitem.title: FRANCE: Metaleurop silent on Glencore plans.
newsitem.headline: Metaleurop silent on Glencore plans.

text.p: Metaleurop declined on Wednesday to comment on news that Switzerland's Glencore group may seek to further raise its equity stake in Metaleurop.
"At this stage it is only a statement of intent, we cannot comment," board member Claus Grosse told reporters.

A newspaper notice detailing the terms Metaleurop's planned 600 million francs capital boost, said that Glencore might seek over the next 12 months to increase its stake in non-ferrous metal group Metaleurop "depending on the evolution of its strategy and of its long-term development in that sector,"
Glencore and Preussag each currently control 25.4 percent stakes in Metaleurop after Glencore exercised an option to buy a 10.4 percent stake in Metaleurop from Preussag.
Both companies have agreed to participate in the capital increase in proportion to their respective stakes.
Preussag currently has 40.48 percent of the voting rights of Metaleurop and Glencore 20.24 percent.
After the capital increase, Preussag will control around 35 percent of the voting rights and Glencore 20 percent, Grosse estimated.

But he explained that from January 1, 1998, Glencore may hold around 30 percent of Metaleurop voting rights and Preussag around 32 percent because Glencore will benefit from double voting rights on shares bought in October 1995.
